chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all of them from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer behind the Imam: Do I recite behind him? He said: 'As for the prayer in which the recitation is not recited aloud, then that has been assigned to him, so do not recite behind him. And as for the one in which it is recited aloud, we have only commanded the aloud recitation so that those behind him may listen. So if you hear, listen; and if you do not hear, then recit.'

key_terms.يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ: In which the recitation is made audible

ai.seo_question: When should a follower recite Surah Al-Fatiha behind the Imam during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the practical application of the principle of *insha'at* (listening attentively) during congregational prayer, distinguishing between *sirr* (silent) and *jahri* (audible) prayers. It establishes that in silent prayers, the follower’s role is purely to listen, whereas in audible prayers, recitation is permitted only if the Imam’s voice is inaudible, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the follower’s active engagement with the Imam’s recitation. This ruling underscores the theological view that the Imam’s recitation suffices for the follower when heard, aligning with the Quranic command to listen when the Quran is recited.
